projects.name: Portsmouth Square Improvement Project
projects.description: ~$73M renovation; pedestrian bridge over Kearny St removed to make room for a larger two-story clubhouse. Park closed for roughly two years from June 2026.

projects.name: Proposition K (Upper Great Highway closure)
projects.location: Upper Great Highway, Lincoln Way to Sloat Blvd
projects.description: Nov 5 2024 ballot measure permanently closing the Upper Great Highway to private cars. Passed citywide 54.73%. Lost ~60-40 in the Sunset and ~70-30 in the Richmond; Districts 1/4/7/11 combined ~61% no.

testimony.speaker: CCBA board member (5 decades)
testimony.claim: Bridge let seniors and children cross Kearny safely; removal harms community access. Never heard the plan from city officials.

testimony.speaker: Merchants association president
testimony.claim: Three simultaneous Chinatown construction projects compound harm to merchants.

testimony.speaker: District 3 Supervisor
testimony.claim: Office received no communication supporting keeping the bridge.

testimony.speaker: Opposition organizer
testimony.claim: Organized opposition never went east of West Portal; most of the city only heard 'a park'.

testimony.speaker: Chinese Cultural Foundation
testimony.claim: The Portsmouth Square Bridge is about Chinatown's history and culture and should not be removed.

testimony.speaker: Architect
testimony.claim: The City has never shown an alternative design keeping the Bridge although the EIR clearly mentioned it.

testimony.speaker: Construction Firm Owner
testimony.claim: If the Portsmouth Square Bridge is removed, the economy in Chinatown is expected to worsen.

testimony.speaker: CCBA Board Member
testimony.claim: The bridge provides a huge open space; the City's claim that removal will create more open spaces doesn't make sense.

testimony.speaker: Kite Shop Owner
testimony.claim: The bridge should not be removed; it is crucial for the community's health and safety.

testimony.speaker: Local Historian
testimony.claim: The bridge represented the financial and civic power that Chinese Americans achieved after World War II despite systemic racism.

testimony.speaker: Local Activists
testimony.claim: Using public money for the bridge was a misallocation of resources that should have gone towards essential housing for residents.

testimony.speaker: Plaintiff
testimony.claim: We feel very confident in our arguments and believe the judge is misreading them.

testimony.speaker: Campaign Consultant
testimony.claim: The way Prop. K was presented was misleading and did not reflect the realities of working-class people who need the highway.

testimony.speaker: Former SFPD Commander
testimony.claim: The organized opposition never informed a large part of the city about the true impacts of Prop. K's closure.

testimony.speaker: Board of Supervisors President
testimony.claim: This measure is divisive and an 'unfunded mandate.'

testimony.speaker: Board of Supervisors member
testimony.claim: Closing the Upper Great Highway could leave the city's Chinese American community feeling isolated.

testimony.speaker: Board of Supervisors member
testimony.claim: Proposition K is a 'once-in-a-century opportunity' to transform the road into an iconic oceanside park that could bring the Sunset to life.

testimony.speaker: Neighborhood Group
testimony.claim: Permanently closing the Upper Great Highway to vehicles could worsen traffic and divert it into residential areas, as well as lengthen commutes.

testimony.speaker: Merchants Association
testimony.claim: These inconveniences would discourage long-time customers from continuing to patronize them.

testimony.speaker: San Francisco Controller's Office
testimony.claim: Maintaining private vehicle access costs the city $350,000 to $700,000 per year for sand removal.

testimony.speaker: SPUR
testimony.claim: Prop. K would help fulfill goals of increasing access to shared public amenities and addressing sea level rise.

testimony.speaker: Trust for Public Land
testimony.claim: Low-income neighborhoods would benefit from enhanced access to open space if Prop. K passes.
